players.product: solder balls and micro solder balls (<130 µm) for BGA / CSP semiconductor packaging

quarterly_data.signal: Half-year report (consolidated, K-IFRS): Q2 2026 revenue KRW 90,753,036,174 vs KRW 57,408,052,168 in Q2 2025; Q2 operating profit KRW 10,078,195,954 vs KRW 2,580,609,710; H1 2026 revenue KRW 159,453,856,342 vs KRW 101,559,099,903; H1 operating profit KRW 9,409,736,905 vs KRW 1,187,991,073; H1 net income KRW 17,616,607,092 vs a loss of KRW 586,982,133. The solder business (metal materials segment, i.e. the parent company: solder balls, powder, paste) had Q2 revenue KRW 57,709,456,340 vs KRW 30,725,786,513 and Q2 operating profit KRW 8,656,577,063 vs KRW 4,655,083,226; H1 revenue KRW 100,341,751,153 vs KRW 56,887,055,618 (FY2025 full year: KRW 126,318,034,393) with H1 operating profit KRW 10,939,345,184 vs KRW 7,750,355,085. Solder H1 sales were KRW 89,254,504K export and KRW 11,087,247K domestic; the solder business was 62.93% of consolidated H1 revenue, the defense/aerospace navigation subsidiary 14.90% (KRW 23,769,259K) and the high-pressure gas-cylinder subsidiary 22.23% (KRW 35,443,904K). The largest customer (customer A, unnamed) bought KRW 32,828,903K = 20.59% of consolidated revenue (H1 2025: KRW 18,653,389K, 18.37%); the top five solder customers are about 49.94% of sales. Separate R&D spend KRW 2,298,254K = 2.29% of sales.

Capacity: the Ulsan solder plants ran 87,510 of 99,912 available hours in H1 2026, 87.6% utilisation (plant 1 solder balls; plant 2 solder balls, solder powder and flux; plant 3 solder paste). The company says it recently expanded its micro solder ball (MSB) plant and production equipment in anticipation of rising downstream demand and is adding equipment flexibly in line with new development and mass-production supply schedules. Solder production cost was KRW 84,705 million in H1 (FY2025: KRW 99,055 million). Parent raw-material inventory rose to KRW 31,189,016K from KRW 8,083,509K at year-end. The company sells on customers' purchase orders and signs no separate order contracts, so it keeps no order backlog.
quarterly_data.figure: H1 2026 utilisation 87.6% (87,510 of 99,912 hours); MSB plant and equipment expanded

quarterly_data.signal: Customers and market position per the half-year report: solder sales go mainly to Samsung Electronics, SK Hynix, STATS ChipPAC Korea, Signetics and Amkor Technology Korea in Korea, and overseas to Samsung Electronics' Suzhou plant, Amkor Assembly & Test (Shanghai) and Amkor Technology Philippines; standing agreements (one-year auto-renewal) are listed with Samsung Electronics (2026), STATS ChipPAC Korea (2023, purchase and supply contract), Amkor Technology Korea (2026), Samsung Electro-Mechanics (2024) and SK Hynix (2026). The company states it holds 60-70% of the Korean solder-ball market and is the No. 2 supplier worldwide, supplies sub-130-micron micro solder balls from what it calls an exclusive position, and names Senju Metal (Japan), MKE (Korea) and Heraeus (Germany) as competitors. R&D in progress: sub-100um micro cored solder balls, low-melting-point cored solder balls, Cu posts of 50um diameter or less, high-reliability LTS solder alloys, low-cost and automotive solder pastes.

Company outlook in the half-year report: it expects stable demand growth to continue as the market grows around AI, HBM and high-performance semiconductors, and is strengthening its solder-ball and related-material technology for advanced packaging; it cites Grand View Research that the global solder-ball semiconductor packaging market grows from about USD 1.94 billion in 2026 to about USD 2.84 billion in 2030.

contracts.signal: Half-year report lists Samsung Electronics (Korea and its Suzhou plant) as a main solder customer and a 2026 agreement set with Samsung Electronics: fair-trade agreement, basic transaction agreement, non-disclosure agreement and quality-assurance agreement, one-year term with automatic renewal.

Half-year report lists SK Hynix as a main solder customer and a 2026 agreement set with SK Hynix: material transaction and basic agreement, non-disclosure agreement and quality-assurance agreement, one-year term with automatic renewal.

Half-year report lists Amkor Technology Korea, Amkor Assembly & Test (Shanghai) and Amkor Technology Philippines as solder customers and a 2026 agreement set with Amkor Technology Korea: standard subcontracting agreement, fair-trade standard agreement and non-disclosure agreement, one-year term with automatic renewal.

Half-year report lists a 2024 agreement set between Duksan Hi-Metal and Samsung Electro-Mechanics among its major contracts: fair-trade agreement and basic transaction agreement, one-year term with automatic renewal.
